extracted.intended_audience: mathematicians, researchers, librarians, and users of mathematical bibliographic/review services
extracted.subtask_description: Describing the standards, scope, and practices of zbMATH Open — an abstracting and reviewing service that produces brief reviews/abstracts and organizes mathematical literature for researchers and librarians. Useful for understanding reviewer selection, coverage, record depth, classification, access, and trade-offs between completeness and timeliness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Comprehensive global coverage objective
rubrics_metrics.description: "Zentralblatt für Mathematik und ihre Grenzgebiete aims to publish—in an efficient and reliable manner—reviews of the entire world literature in mathematics and related areas."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This expresses the service's overarching standard: aim to cover the global mathematical literature. The sentence further implies obligations of breadth (entire world literature), efficiency, and reliability in publication. It also notes that areas closely related to mathematics should be treated as seriously as pure mathematics.

rubrics_metrics.name: Review content standard — brief accounts of contents
rubrics_metrics.description: "The Zentralblatt MATH abstracting service provides reviews (brief accounts of contents) of current articles, conference papers, books and other publications in mathematics, its applications, and related areas."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviews are expected to be concise summaries focused on the contents of the work. Guidance in the article: reviews are predominantly in English with occasional German and French; formats covered include journal articles, conference papers, and books. This informs expectations about language, scope, and the typical length/role of reviews (abstracting rather than full critique).

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of Mathematics Subject Classification (MSC) codes
rubrics_metrics.description: "It uses the Mathematics Subject Classification codes for organising reviews by topic."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Organizational standard: all records/reviews are indexed/classified using MSC codes to group items by mathematical topic, which affects discoverability and topical curation of reviews.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reviewer selection criterion — invited volunteers
rubrics_metrics.description: "Reviewers are volunteers invited by the editors based on their published work or a recommendation by an existing reviewer."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Standard for reviewer qualification and recruitment: reviewers are selected (not self-appointed) and chosen for demonstrated published work or via recommendation, implying expertise-based selection. Also implies a volunteer (unpaid) model and editorial oversight in invitations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Record depth standard (index, abstracts, reviews)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specifies the kinds of metadata/record content provided per item: at minimum indexing and abstracts, with fuller entries including reviews. This clarifies what users can expect in a record and how richly items are described.

rubrics_metrics.name: Coverage breadth — journals, serials, books, proceedings
rubrics_metrics.description: "The service reviews more than 2,300 journals and serials worldwide, as well as books and conference proceedings."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Operational coverage standard: the service aims to include a very large set of serials plus non-serial outputs. This sets expectations for scope (journals, books, proceedings) and can be used to evaluate whether an item type should be included.

rubrics_metrics.name: Temporal and archival coverage expectation
rubrics_metrics.description: Statements such as "Temporal coverage: 1868–present (first entry from 1755)" and "the database also incorporates the 200,000 entries of the earlier similar publication Jahrbuch ... from 1868 to 1942".
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sets an archival completeness standard: zbMATH aims to maintain long historical coverage and incorporate legacy databases to provide historical records. This affects expectations about backfile coverage and retrospective inclusion of older literature.

rubrics_metrics.name: Access policy — open access availability
rubrics_metrics.description: "As of January 2021, the complete database is accessible for free."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specifies an access standard/policy: full open access to the database as of the stated date. The page also contrasts prior access limits (previously only the first three records in a search were available without a subscription), indicating a shift toward full openness as a normative state.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scope principle — treat related areas seriously
rubrics_metrics.description: "As the name suggests, the main focus of the journal is mathematics. However, those areas that are closely related to mathematics will be treated as seriously as the so-called pure mathematics."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Scope criterion: while mathematics is primary, applications and closely related fields must receive comparable editorial seriousness. This guides inclusion decisions and review attitude toward interdisciplinary work.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timeliness vs documentary completeness trade-off (anti-pattern)
rubrics_metrics.description: From the Jahrbuch historical note: "The Jahrbuch's founding concept was characterized by its documentary completeness. The Jahrbuch only appeared when all papers in a year had been completely processed. This was later paid for with a great loss of relevance."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Operational lesson/anti-pattern: insisting on absolute documentary completeness and publishing only when everything is processed can render a reviewing service irrelevant; zbMATH (Zentralblatt) emphasized faster publication frequency to maintain relevance. This functions as guidance to prioritize timeliness alongside completeness.
